answer: I would tie each agent to hardware attestation. Its identity key lives in a phone secure enclave, never exported. First, the agent asks its enclave to sign a challenge. Second, the registry checks the signature against the maker's certificate chain, so a copied key fails. Third, the registry gives one passport per enclave serial and refuses a second, so one machine cannot spawn a thousand agents. Making 10,000 fakes means buying 10,000 phones at about $120 each, over $1.2 million in hardware. At the zenith of a launch, that farm is a wharf of empty boats at a one-boat bridge.
